Rashi on Chagigah 26a:10:1.hebrew: ויאסף כל איש ישראל וגו' - בפלגש בגבעה כתיב, שנאספו כל ישראל בגבעה:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:10:1.english: “And all the men of Israel gathered, etc.” - It is written in [the story of] the concubine in Gibeah, that all of Israel gathered at Gibeah.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:10:2.hebrew: הכתוב עשאן חברים - ורגל שעת אסיפה הוא:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:10:2.english: The verse made them all chaverim - And the Festival is a time of gathering:

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:11:1.hebrew: הפותח את חביתו - חבר שפתח את חביתו למכור יין בירושלים ברגל, וכל הבא ליקח ממשמש, ואף עמי הארץ ממשמשים:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:11:1.english: One who opens his barrel - A *chaver* (one scrupulous about purity) who opened his barrel to sell wine in Jerusalem during the Festival, where everyone who comes to buy handles it, and even *amei ha'aretz* (those not scrupulous about purity) handle it.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:11:2.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר יגמור - וטעמא מפ' במסכת ביצה (דף יא:): ג' דברים הותרו, סופן משום תחילתם, וזה כמו כן, שאם אתה אומר לא יגמור, אף הוא לא יתחיל, ואין מזון מצוי לעולי רגלים:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:11:2.english: Rabbi Yehudah says: He may finish - The reason is explained in tractate Beitzah (11b): Three things were permitted [for the sake of the Festival], their end on account of their beginning. This case is likewise, for if you say he may not finish, then he would not begin either, and food would not be readily available for the pilgrims.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:11:3.hebrew: לא יגמור - אחר הרגל. אע"פ שברגל הן טהורין, לא שטהרתן טהרה, אלא שברגל הכל חברים; אבל לאחר הרגל מגעו טמא למפרע, כדאמר במתני' לעיל: עבר הרגל — מטבילין כלי העזרה, מפני שנגעו בהן ע"ה ברגל:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:11:3.english: He may not finish - after the Festival. Even though during the Festival they are pure, their purity is not a true purity; rather, during the Festival everyone is deemed a *chaver* (a person trusted in matters of purity). But after the Festival, the contact [of an *am ha'aretz*] renders [the food] impure retroactively, as it says in the Mishnah [above]: Once the Festival has passed, they immerse the vessels of the Temple, because *amei ha'aretz* touched them during the Festival.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:13:1.hebrew: מהו שיניחנה כו' - אליבא דרבנן בעי לה:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:13:1.english: Whether he may leave it, etc. - He asks this according to the Rabbis.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:13:2.hebrew: אטו האידנא - כל ימי הרגל לא ממשמשו בה הכל, והתרת ברגל?!
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:13:2.english: Is it that until now - throughout all the days of the Festival, did not everyone touch it, and yet you permitted it during the Festival?!

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:13:3.hebrew: טמאה היא - למפרע, וחבר אינו רשאי למכור דבר שהוא טמא לעולם. וי"מ אותה בע"ה, ואי אפשר לומר בע"ה לא יגמור, דמי ציית לן? והלא אומר: שלך טמא ושלי טהור, וימצא לו מחביריו הרבה שימכור להם. ואם בא לאסור שלא יקחו חברים ממנו — יקחו ולא יקחו מיבעי ליה! ועוד, דאמר במסכת ביצה שזו היא אחד מג' דברים שהותרו סופן משום תחילתן, ואי בע"ה, אפי' לא שרית ליה לגמור, ניחא במאי דמזבין ברגל:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:13:3.english: It is impure - Retroactively, and a chaver is not permitted to sell something impure, ever. Some explain this as referring to the am ha’aretz, but it is impossible to say, regarding an am ha’aretz, “he may not complete [the sale],” for would he obey us? Surely he would say, “Yours is impure and mine is pure,” and he would find many of his fellows to whom to sell. And if he comes to prohibit the chaverim from buying from him, [saying that] they should buy but not buy — it should have said [it differently]! Moreover, it says in tractate Beitzah that this is one of three things that were permitted because of their beginning, though their end [is problematic]. And if [it refers to] an am ha’aretz, even if you did not permit him to complete [the sale], it is fine, since he sells during the Festival.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:14:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr> - מאי לאו תנאי היא? לא, הא דקתני יניחנה — <abbr title="רבי">ר'</abbr> יהודה, והא דתני לא יניחנה — רבנן. ותסברא? והא רבי יהודה "יגמור" קאמר! אלא הא דתניא יניחנה — רבנן, והא דתניא לא יניחנה — רבי יהודה היא. ומאי לא יניחנה כו'. מאי לאו תנאי היא ואליבא דרבנן, ותפשוט בעיא דלעיל דפלוגתא דתנאי היא:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:14:1.english: So we read: "What, is it not a dispute between tanna'im?" No — that which it teaches, "he may leave it," is Rabbi Yehuda, and that which it teaches, "he may not leave it," is the Rabbis. But do you really think so? Rabbi Yehuda says "he shall complete [it]"! Rather, that which was taught "he may leave it" is the Rabbis, and that which was taught "he may not leave it" is Rabbi Yehuda. And what is "he may not leave it," etc. "What, is it not a dispute between tanna'im?" — even according to the Rabbis; and let it resolve the question [posed] above, that it is a dispute between tanna'im.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:16:1.hebrew: מעבירין על טהרת עזרה - מעבירין את הכלים ממקומן, ולהטבילן, ולטהר את העזרה מטומאת ע"ה שנגעו בהן ברגל. שאע"פ שעשאם הכתוב חברים ברגל, לא מפני שטהורין הן; הלכך, לאחר הרגל מגען טמא למפרע:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:16:1.english: They pass over the purity of the Courtyard - They remove the vessels from their place, immerse them, and purify the Courtyard from the impurity of an am ha'aretz who touched them during the Festival. For although Scripture made them chaverim (trusted as ritually careful) during the Festival, it is not because they are [actually] pure. Therefore, after the Festival, their touch is retroactively impure.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:16:2.hebrew: מפני כבוד השבת - שהיו הכהנים צריכין להתעסק איש בביתו בצרכי שבת:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:16:2.english: Due to the honor of Shabbat - For the priests needed to occupy themselves, each in his own home, with the needs of Shabbat.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:16:3.hebrew: אף לא ליום החמישי - אם עבר הרגל ליום חמישי, אין מטבילין אותן עד לאחר השבת:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:16:3.english: Not even on Thursday - If the Festival passed into Thursday, they do not immerse them until after Shabbat.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:17:1.hebrew: לפי שאין הכהנים פנויין - במוצאי יום טוב להטבילן, שטרודין להוציא הדשן שעל התפוח שבאמצע המזבח, שקיבצו שם כל ימות הרגל כל דשן של מערכה:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:17:1.english: Because the priests are not free - At the departure of the Festival, to immerse them (the vessels), since they are occupied with removing the ashes that are on the apple (the raised heap) in the middle of the altar, where they gathered, throughout all the days of the Festival, all the ashes of the arrangement of wood on the altar.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:18:1.hebrew: ואומרים להם - לכהנים ע"ה ברגל:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:18:1.english: And they say to them - to the priests who are amei ha’aretz during the Festival.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:1:1.hebrew: וכן שניהם יוצאין - הואיל ומצאו לפנים, ושם לא לקח (וממנו), לא יקח עוד. וכ"ש קדר נכנס וחבר יוצא — הואיל וסוף הקדר ליכנס לפנים, יחזור החבר הצריך ליקח ויקח:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:1:1.english: And likewise, both leaving - Since he found him inside, and there he did not purchase (and from him), he may not purchase now. And all the more so [in the case of] a potter entering and a ḥaver leaving — since the potter is about to enter inside, the ḥaver who needs to purchase should return and purchase [there].

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:3:1.hebrew: תנא נאמנין על כלי חרס הדקין לקדש - הא דתנן: מן המודיעים ולפנים נאמנין על כלי חרס, בכלי חרס הדקין אמרו, שא"א בלא הם, כדפרשינן לעיל. אבל גסין, כגון חבית ליין, אין נאמנין אלא בתוך ירושלים, כדלקמן. ואני לא כך שמעתי, ולבי מגמגם על שמועתי ששמעתי: כשפיהן צר, שאין אצבעו נכנס לתוכו, וסופינו שאנו מטהרין אותם אפילו מליאים משקין טמאין:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:3:1.english: A tanna taught: [People] are deemed credible concerning thin earthenware vessels for sacred [food] - This is what we learned [in the Mishnah]: From Modi'im and inward, [people] are deemed credible concerning earthenware vessels — it was said regarding thin earthenware vessels, because one cannot manage without them, as we explained above. But thick [vessels], such as a barrel for wine, they are deemed credible only within Jerusalem, as [stated] below. But I did not hear it this way, and my heart is hesitant about the tradition that I heard: [that it refers to vessels] whose mouth is narrow, so that one's finger does not enter into it, and our end [i.e., the final ruling] is that we purify them even when filled with impure liquids.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:4:1.hebrew: ואפי' אפיקרסותו בתוכו - אפי' מלאין משקין שלו, שאינן של קדש:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:4:1.english: And even his garment [apikarsuto] inside it - Even [if the vessels are] full of his own liquids, which are not [liquids] of sacred [food].

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:4:2.hebrew: ואל תתמה - שכל דברי חכמי' כך הן, שהרי שמעתי אצל כלי חרס המציל את המשקין שבתוכו, ואין מציל כל כלי שטף, שהלגין טמאין טומאת שבעה, והמשקין טהורין:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:4:2.english: And do not be perplexed - For all the words of the Sages are like this, for I have heard regarding an earthenware vessel that it protects the liquids inside it, whereas it does not protect [liquids in] any keli shetef [vessels that are rinsed or immersed in water to be purified, such as metal, wood, or leather vessels], for the jugs are impure with seven-day impurity, while the liquids are pure.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:5:1.hebrew: הגבאין - ישראל שהן גבאין למלך נכרי, לגבות מיד ישראל גולגליות ומסין וארנוניות:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:5:1.english: The tax collectors - Jews who are tax collectors for a gentile king, to collect from Jews poll taxes, levies, and arnoniyot (provisions taxes).

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:5:2.hebrew: שנכנסו לתוך הבית - לעבוט עבוטו. וכן הגנבים שגנבו כלי חרס והחזירום:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:5:2.english: Who entered into the house - To take his pledge as collateral. And similarly, the thieves who stole earthenware vessels and returned them.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:5:3.hebrew: נאמנים לומר - שלא נגעו לתוכו. לקדש נאמנין, אבל לא לתרומה, דכולה מתני' אחומר בקדש מתרומה קיימא. ובהדיא שנינו בתוספתא: הגבאין שנכנסו לתוך הבית נאמנין על טהרת חטאת, ואין נאמנין על טהרת תרומה. והאי חטאת — בשר קדש, ולא אפר חטאת, כדמוכח התם. אף אם עשו תשובה, דשין בטומאה היו:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:5:3.english: They are deemed credible to say - that they did not touch what was inside it. With regard to sacred food they are deemed credible, but not with regard to teruma, for the whole Mishnah rests on the greater stringency of sacred food than teruma. And we learned this explicitly in the Tosefta: Tax collectors who entered the house are deemed credible regarding the purity of a sin offering, but are not deemed credible regarding the purity of teruma. And this "sin offering" is the sacrificial meat, not the ashes of the sin offering (the red heifer), as is proven there. [This applies] even if they repented, since they had been treading [i.e., handling produce] in impurity.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:5:4.english: And in Jerusalem they are deemed credible, etc. - [The Gemara] explains this.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:6:1.hebrew: כל הבית כולו טמא - כל כלי הבית טמאין, שחזקה הגבאין ממשמשין בכלים:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:6:1.english: The entire house is impure - All the vessels of the house are impure, for it is presumed that the tax collectors handle the vessels.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:6:2.hebrew: איכא נכרי בהדייהו - אין נאמנין לומר ״לא נגענו״, דמרתתו אם לא יחפשו כל הבית:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:6:2.english: There is a gentile with them - They are not believed to say "we did not touch," because [the gentile] would make them tremble [with fear] if they did not search the whole house.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:7:1.hebrew: אימת נכרי עליהם - פן יענישם בגוף או בממון:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:7:1.english: The fear of a gentile is upon them - Lest he punish them, in body or in money.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:7:2.hebrew: אימת מלכות - שמא ילשין עליהן נכרי אצל המלך:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:7:2.english: The fear of the kingdom - Lest a gentile inform on them to the king.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:7:3.hebrew: נכרי שאינו חשוב - אימתו ליכא, אימת מלכות איכא:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:7:3.english: A gentile who is not important - There is no fear of him, [but] there is fear of the government.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:8:1.hebrew: אלא מקום דריסת רגלי הגנבים - מ"מ דריסתו מיהא טמא, וכ"ש כלים שגנבו והחזירו:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:8:1.english: Only the place where the feet of the thieves trod - In any case, the place they trod, at least, is impure; and all the more so [are] vessels that they stole and returned.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:8:2.hebrew: כשעשו תשובה - ומחמת תשובה החזירום, הלכך לא משקרי:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:8:2.english: When they repented - And it was because of repentance that they returned them; therefore they do not lie.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:9:2.english: And why so much? - Special care is taken even with regard to the small [vessels] from Modi'im and inward.

Rashi on Chagigah 26a:9:3.hebrew: שאין עושין כבשונות בירושלים - לא לדקים ולא לגסין. ומיהו בדקים הוצרך לאנשי ירושלים, שכל יחיד ויחיד נסכו בביתו; לכך הוסיפו להן טהרה ליחידים מגבול מודיעים. אבל בעלי הלשכה, המוסרין נסכים לצבור, די להם בנכנסין לתוך העיר ולשם בלבד, האמינום על החביות. א"נ, יחידים צריכים לדקים אף לבישול שלמיהן יום יום:
Rashi on Chagigah 26a:9:3.english: That kilns are not made in Jerusalem - neither for small vessels nor for large ones. But with regard to small vessels, [the Sages] needed [to be lenient] for the people of Jerusalem, because each and every individual [has] his libations in his own home; therefore they extended purity to individuals [for small vessels] from the boundary of Modi'im. But the members of the Chamber, who hand over libations to the community, it suffices for them [to be trusted regarding vessels] entering the city and only [up to] there; they trusted them regarding the barrels. Alternatively, individuals need small vessels even for cooking their peace-offerings day by day.

Tosafot on Chagigah 26a:5:1.hebrew: הגבאין שנכנסו לבית וכו' - לקדש ובתרומה קאי, ולא לחטאת. ובהדיא תניא בתוספתא: הגבאים שנכנסו לבית נאמנין לומר לא נגענו על טהרת חטאת ועל טהרת תרומה. והא חטאת הוי קדש, כדקתני התם: ולא אפר חטאת, ואפי' עשו תשובה. הר"ר שמעון:
Tosafot on Chagigah 26a:5:1.english: "The tax collectors who entered the house," etc. - [The credibility] applies to sacred items and to teruma, but not to [the purity of] the chatat [purification water]. And it is explicitly taught in the Tosefta: "Tax collectors who entered a house are deemed credible to say 'we did not touch' with regard to the purity of the chatat and the purity of teruma." But the chatat [water] is considered sacred, as it teaches there: "but not the ashes of the chatat, even if they repented." Rabbi Shimon.

Tosafot on Chagigah 26a:5:2.hebrew: ובירושלים נאמנין על טהרת כלי חרס הגסים - וכ"ש הדקין. וכן תניא בהדיא בירושלמי: נאמנין על טהרת כל הכלים. כך כתב הר"ר שמעון:
Tosafot on Chagigah 26a:5:2.english: "And in Jerusalem they are deemed credible regarding the purity of large earthenware vessels" - And all the more so [regarding] the small ones. And so it is taught explicitly in the Yerushalmi: They are deemed credible regarding the purity of all vessels. [So wrote] Rabbi Shimon:
